arguments.value: 13-year-old female with recurrent suprasellar pilocytic astrocytoma (WHO grade I) associated with partial hypopituitarism and cranial diabetes insipidus, initially presenting at age 2 and later developing progressive leptomeningeal dissemination to the brain and spine despite prior partial resection, chemotherapy, and VP shunt placement. At age 13 she re-presented with raised intracranial pressure, seizures, and worsening mass effect; repeat surgery confirmed pilocytic astrocytoma, but follow-up imaging showed further leptomeningeal spread, and she died shortly thereafter at home.
